# Veltkamp's split

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `split` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$a$, exactly:

$$a_h + a_l = a.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`two_prod_dekker`](two_prod_dekker.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $a_h + a_l = a$ exactly.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `split_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Split.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Split.v), against `split_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition split_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (4 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  let '(ah, al) := split emin prec tie_even a in
  fmt emin prec ah /\
  fmt emin prec al /\
  (ah + al) = a.
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** Veltkamp's split (Dekker 1971). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/split.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/split.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/Model.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# Veltkamp's split: a = ah + al exactly, with ah on the upper half of the precision. Used by
# Dekker's product. Proved from precision 4 on (the source's condition on the splitter's
# exponent); exhaustive runs find it true from precision 1.

g  = prod(const splitter, a)
d  = sub(a, g)
ah = add(g, d)
al = sub(a, ah)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#split)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 60 885 344 | 0 | 0 (exact) |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 59 523 208 | 0 | 0 (exact) |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 1 213 903 | 0 | 0 (exact) |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
